title: Paste As Plain Text Does Not Play Well With Sticky Keys
summary: Investigate the low-confidence modifier-restore ordering hypothesis with controlled maintainer reproduction. Both accessibility Sticky Keys-enabled and disabled cases are reported; the supplied snapshots do not establish physical release timing or Keyboard Manager causality.

next_action.reason: The code permits a plausible stale-restore ordering, but it has not been captured in an incident.
next_action.label: Reproduce modifier restoration timing

judgment.rationale: Investigate the low-confidence modifier-restore ordering hypothesis with controlled maintainer reproduction. Both accessibility Sticky Keys-enabled and disabled cases are reported; the supplied snapshots do not establish physical release timing or Keyboard Manager causality.
evidence: Original 0.71 report uses sequential Win, Ctrl, Alt, V with Windows Sticky Keys enabled.
The detailed 0.101.2362 report records LWin/LAlt logically down after direct Alt+Win+V paste, later all up; the required physical-release ordering was not captured.
Keyboard Manager with LWin+V to LCtrl+V was enabled and not isolated in that report.
November 17 commenter says Sticky Keys are not enabled in their case.

Read the restore helper and complete direct-paste input batch, plus the detached action dispatch: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/00d85a4c73c2ec33da7a9c25d1a3581b3d4c4359/src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPasteModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp
Read the original Sticky Keys screenshot: enabled, lock modifiers when pressed twice, and do not turn off when two keys are pressed simultaneously.
Read related #43220, #42471 and #50127. They corroborate modifier latching, but do not establish this timing mechanism or a covering implementation.
Read the closure discussion: #25678 was redirected to #33773, whose final comment redirects to this issue. These are duplicate-routing closures, not a shipped fix.
Bounded issue-number and symptom searches found no issue-specific upstream/fork implementation; unrelated Advanced Paste feature mirrors are not treated as coverage.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the bounded release-timing and Keyboard Manager/Sticky Keys matrix before approving any corrective modifier-restoration change.

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional restore-order direction is applicable, but no incident proves the race. Existing duplicate closures do not identify a fixing implementation. Retain the red-confidence hypothesis and a concrete maintainer reproduction action instead of asking the reporter to instrument native code.

proposed_fixes.title: Conditionally correct modifier restoration after release-timing investigation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: synthetic modifier key-down restoration can be queued before physical release and submitted afterwards; the incident ordering and Keyboard Manager contribution remain unproven.
plan: Instrument modifier-only restore decisions and requested/sent input counts, without reading typed text or clipboard content.
Force release timing around restore sampling/submission; compare Keyboard Manager off/on and Sticky Keys off/on independently.
If stale restoration is proven, correct modifier ownership/release ordering without releasing genuinely held keys.
Add focused release-before-submit and sequential-Sticky-Keys tests.
verification: All released modifiers return up after plain-text paste across controlled timing cases.
Genuinely held modifiers and existing remaps retain their behavior.

reproduce.title: Verify Advanced Paste report
reproduce.version_requirement: 0.101.2362 and current supported build; compare original Sticky Keys sequence
prerequisites: Disposable Windows test session, Advanced Paste enabled, harmless sample text and Notepad.
Record the PowerToys/Windows build; compare reported 0.101.2362 with a current supported build.
Maintainer-native diagnostics limited to modifier states, timestamps and requested/sent input counts; no typed text or clipboard content.
setup: Set direct paste to Alt+Win+V and compare Keyboard Manager disabled against the supplied LWin+V remap.
Use an isolated test session; do not disable endpoint protection or collect typed text/clipboard contents.
Compare Keyboard Manager disabled/enabled as a controlled variable, without changing security software.
Record only restore decisions, requested/sent input counts and modifier-state snapshots; never capture typed text or clipboard content.
steps: 1. Copy harmless text, set direct paste to Alt+Win+V, and with Sticky Keys and Keyboard Manager off vary when physical Alt/Win are released around paste.
2. Repeat with the reported LWin+V to LCtrl+V remap enabled; record physical release, restore sampling/submission order and logical states separately.
3. Independently enable Sticky Keys with double-press locking enabled and two-key auto-disable off. Copy with Ctrl+C, then press and release Win, Ctrl, Alt, V one at a time as in the original report.
4. Compare released versus genuinely held modifiers after paste, and verify any tap-to-clear recovery without treating an absent snapshot as continuous latching.
reproduce.expected_result: Released modifiers do not remain logically latched, while physically held keys and intentional Sticky Keys behavior are preserved.

issue_context.summary: Direct plain-text paste sometimes leaves shortcut modifiers logically held. The original sequential Sticky Keys report and newer simultaneous-shortcut reports need separate reproduction tracks.
known_information: Original 0.71 report uses sequential Win, Ctrl, Alt, V with Windows Sticky Keys enabled.
The detailed 0.101.2362 report records LWin/LAlt logically down after direct Alt+Win+V paste, later all up; the required physical-release ordering was not captured.

inferences: Hypothesis: synthetic modifier key-down restoration can be queued before physical release and submitted afterwards; the incident ordering and Keyboard Manager contribution remain unproven.
issue_context.analysis: The direct action runs on a detached worker. It samples modifier state while building key-down restore events, then submits the input batch later. Release between sampling and submission could reassert a released modifier, but public snapshots capture only logical state. The original accessibility configuration enables Sticky Keys and double-press locking; the October follow-up and latest commenter report Sticky Keys disabled. Neither Keyboard Manager nor security software is established as the cause.
